1970.notes: Pre-1971 schedule (the Oklahoma Income Tax Act of 1971 applies only to years after Dec 31, 1970). ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1970-71 ed. (report M-57), Table 36 (pp. 79-80), rates as of December 31, 1970, i.e. the law for tax year 1970 as it ended; the 1969 edition (M-50, Table 40, December 31, 1969) prints the same schedule. Single schedule 1% on the first $1,500 to 6% over $7,500; joint brackets are double the single ones (ACIR note: the income classes shown are for individuals and heads of households, twice as large for joint returns). Federal income tax paid was deductible in computing net income (ACIR 'Federal tax deductible'); not modelled. Deduction is the $1,000 per-person exemption only (Table 37, p. 83; $500 per dependent); the standard deduction (10% of income, $1,000 maximum single or joint, $500 married filing separately; Table 38, p. 85) depends on income and is left out as in later years.

1981.notes: Method 1 schedule (taxpayer not deducting federal income tax). Method 2 let taxpayers deduct federal income tax and use a steeper schedule up to 17%; not modelled. Oklahoma Tax Commission Annual Report, fiscal year ended June 30, 1982 (Internet Archive state-documents microfiche, PDF page index 7, 'Review of 1981-82 taxes and collections'): Method I 'Single: from 1/2 of 1% of the first $1,000 of taxable income and graduated up to 6% of income over $7,500. Married: from 1/2 of 1% of the first $2,000 ... up to 6% of income over $15,000'; head of household uses married rates; 'Personal exemption: $750 each. Effective with 1982 returns payable in 1983, the personal exemption is $1,000.' So the $750 exemption applied to 1981 returns (filed during FY1981-82); the FY1980-81 report (micro_IA40706909_0384, page n7) states the same schedule and $750. Deduction is the $750 per-person exemption only; the standard deduction (15% of Oklahoma AGI, $1,000 min / $2,000 max; MFS $500-$1,000) depends on income and is left out. Bracket steps are those printed in the 1980 and 1983 ACIR tables (this file's 1980 and 1983 entries); the FY1981-FY1984 Tax Commission reports all describe the same 1/2%-6% over $7,500 schedule and 68 O.S. 2355 was not amended between Laws 1980, c. 288 and Laws 1985, c. 179/200.
